newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: ASEAN gas pipeline seen to cost $150 bln-study.
newsitem.headline: ASEAN gas pipeline seen to cost $150 bln-study.

text.p: A trans-ASEAN gas transmission system is estimated to require $150 billion in investments over a 20-year period, a study by the ASEAN-European Commission Energy Management Training and Research Centre (AEEMTRC) showed.
The amount covers financing for the building of pipelines and new stations along with the exploration of new fields, the AEEMTRC study said.
The Jakarta-based AEEMTRC is one of the main implementing agencies for energy cooperation in the ASEAN as well as between ASEAN and the European Union.

The study, completed and submitted to the ASEAN (Association of Southeast Asian Nations) energy ministers last year did not include Vietnam along with three new members - Laos, Cambodia and Myanmar - as the study started prior to their joining the group.
The study cited several possible routes for the proposed gas pipeline which will run from Thailand to Malaysia then to Singapore, Indonesia, Brunei then to the Philippines.
The study said agreements should be sought between gas companies or governments which will include issues such as pricing, financing, sovereign guaranties, transit rights and dispute settlement.
The study estimated ASEAN proven gas reserves at 3,724 billion cubic metres with probable additional reserves of 2,253 bcm. -- Manila newsroom (632) 8418939 Fax 8176267
